_meta: Plain-English definitions for tap-to-explain terms (components/Term.tsx) and /learn/glossary. Keep each 'short' under ~30 words and free of numbers that go stale.

ev.short: Electric vehicle. On this site it covers fully electric cars and plug-in hybrids, unless we say 'fully electric'.

bev.short: Runs only on a battery you charge by plugging in. No gas engine, no gas tank, no oil changes.

phev.short: A battery you plug in for roughly 20–50 electric miles, then a gas engine takes over. Saves money only if you actually plug it in.

hybrid.short: A gas car with a small battery that helps the engine and recharges itself. It never plugs in (a Prius, or today's Camry).

fast-charger.short: Public high-power chargers, mostly along highways. A typical stop takes the battery from about 10% to 80% in 20–45 minutes, but costs several times home electricity.

level1.short: An ordinary 120-volt household outlet and the cord that comes with the car. Slow — about 40 miles overnight — but it's free and enough for many commutes.

level2.short: A 240-volt charger (the kind of outlet a clothes dryer uses), installed by an electrician. Refills most EVs overnight.

kwh.short: The unit your power bill charges for — electricity's version of a gallon. Most EVs go about 3 miles on one.

cents-per-kwh.short: What your utility charges for one kWh of electricity — like the price per gallon at the pump.

range.short: How far an EV goes on a full charge in the government's standard test. Real trips vary with speed, hills, and weather.

winter-range.short: Our estimate for a freezing West Virginia day, when heating the cabin and a cold battery cut range by roughly a quarter.

highway-range.short: How far it goes at a steady 70 mph in mild weather. Lower than the EPA number because wind resistance rises with speed.

efficiency.short: How much electricity it uses to go 100 miles. Lower is better — the EV version of higher mpg.

battery.short: How much energy the battery holds — the size of the 'tank.' Bigger usually means more range, and a longer charge.

tou.short: A utility rate that charges less for electricity at night and on weekends, in exchange for charging then. Some require a separate EV meter.

resale.short: What the car is worth when you sell it, as a share of its sticker price. Early EVs lost value fast; nobody knows yet how today's will do, so we show a range.

msrp.short: The manufacturer's suggested price. Dealers often sell for less (or more). Destination is the delivery fee added to every new car.

frunk.short: Extra storage in an EV: a front trunk where a gas engine would be, and often a hidden bin under the rear cargo floor.

one-pedal.short: Lifting off the pedal slows the car by turning the motor into a generator, putting energy back in the battery — so brake pads last much longer.

wv-ev-fee.short: West Virginia charges fully electric cars an extra yearly registration fee (less for plug-in hybrids) because they pay no gas tax.
